title: Promoter Paddy Harmon, Dreamland and the municipal pier
summary: Harmon publicized the band and ran Dreamland and the pier, where the band moved after Labor Day.

story.theme_name: Dance halls, lake camps and riverboat bandstands
story.community_name: Dance halls, lake resorts and where bands played

blocks.x: Of course, we had good fortune of having a man who was a wonderful promoter, Patty Harmon.
Oh, yes, I must have asked about that.
And he did all the publicizing of our outfit. In fact, he was the making of the outfit because we had the orchestra pictures all over the L station.
I took some pictures of that 20 years ago.
The old Harmon's Greenland out on Palina.
And you were in the back.
Then we'd go from one job to the other because he was running the pier. At that time it was called a municipal pier.
Is that where the Navy pier is?
That's where the Navy pier is now. At that time he had the contract with the city to run it. We'd go from Dreamland on Sunday before Labor Day and move over to the pier on Labor Day.
Stay there in the winter then?

That's good. See if there's any more questions here about these early days. It's mostly the early days that we're asking about because a lot of the later things we could read in the newspapers and the magazines and downbeat. Yeah. Back before they had a downbeat for instance.
